name: Brutalist Web Design
visualIdentity: Explicitly described as a web-design treatment, distinct from architectural Brutalism. Combines web screenshots, bold type, raw interface fragments, hard-edged blocks and deliberately mismatched media. Keep a clear information order; favor direct cuts, scrolling and rough collage while keeping text readable and glitches meaningful.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to raw, direct sites and promos. Suggested fits include indie launches, zines, culture sites, design critiques, product teardowns and dev logs. The catalog also lists editorial narratives, product explainers, evidence sequences, comparisons and motion posters. Suitability is inferred from these examples; use the style where abrasive presentation supports the message.
limitations: Avoid unreadable text, meaningless glitches and over-annotation. Omit glitch cuts in calm editorial scenes or when distortion harms communication. Card stacks must not hide essential copy, provenance or comparison labels; carousels are poor for long reading or simultaneous comparison. Do not force chapter transitions into short topics or obscure causal relationships.
palette: Suggested fallback tokens are white #FFFFFF background, black #000000 foreground and lime #CEFF24 accent; these are suggestions, not canonical requirements. Preserve supplied, brand and approved colors, role assignments, asset colors and style color limits. Use discrete colors; gradients are disabled. Black on white is listed at 21:1 and black on lime at 17.954:1, but check actual compositing and text readability; two-color ratios do not guarantee accessibility.
motionAndInteraction: Use hard cuts, scrolling and rough collage. Optional patterns include scroll-led card stacking, chapter handoffs, horizontal swipe carousels, staged storytelling and brief glitch cuts. Interactive versions may use scroll, swipe, buttons or keyboard; keep backward states coherent, provide reading holds and reduced-motion behavior where applicable. For video, author the same states on a deterministic, seekable timeline; do not rely on live input. Keep dimensions and typography stable, and avoid flashing or persistent distortion.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voiceover, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied audio choices and assets. Keep speech intelligible, avoid clipping or competing vocals, synchronize sound and picture, and inspect them together.
assetRequirements: Layer screenshots, transparent assets and real text directly; retain stable asset dimensions and typography. Use authorized media and exact copy. For screenshot galleries, use accurate image dimensions and responsive sources, meaningful alternatives, keyboard access and fallback links. SVG annotations can use black or lime ink, with readable body text; optional photocopy imagery should use fixed grain.
combinations: Suggested hybrids: style-054 photocopy imagery can unify mismatched screenshots and photos; keep lime, fixed grain and clear hierarchy. Style-024 annotations can add explanatory black or lime arrows and circles; point before adding a note and avoid clutter. Motion patterns are optional: stacks, chapter transitions, carousels and storytelling should fit the content; glitch cuts suit abrasive digital transitions only. These are catalog suggestions, not required pairings.
productionApproach: Choose visual construction and motion tools for the style and action; HTML/CSS and Canvas 2D are listed for rendering, with GSAP for authored motion. HyperFrames is the default composition, timing, synchronization, validation and export pipeline; use Remotion only if it is unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability, recording the reason. Keep video state seekable and deterministic. For interactive HTML, live scroll and pointer behavior may drive interaction; keep one owner per animated property. Audio is selected separately and assembled with picture.
